Well, I've been farming these 5 mu for a long time — my father farmed them before me. At 68, I'm not going to change much. My two sons work in town most of the year, so it's mostly me and my wife in the field, and the grandkids help during busy times like wheat harvest and maize planting.

The wheat is already in the ground — I planted it back in early October like I always do. Now I'm mostly thinking about the spring topdressing and then the quick turnaround to maize in June. Five mu isn't much, but with seven mouths at home it matters. We eat some of the wheat and maize ourselves, sell the rest at the local grain station.

For fertilizer I use compound fertilizer (复合肥) as base and urea for topdressing. The extension fellow came by a few years back and said 15 kg urea per mu was enough for wheat, but honestly I put down a bit more because the year I tried less my wheat looked pale at jointing and I got scared. Better to spend a few extra yuan than risk the yield. For maize I use less — the summer rains usually help.

Irrigation: I have a share in the village tube well. Wheat needs it — I water at green-up in spring, at jointing, and at grain-filling if it's dry. Maize I only water if June-July is dry, because the rains usually come.

I don't buy fancy hybrid seed every year for wheat — I save some from last year's harvest and buy a bag of the local improved variety to mix in. For maize I buy hybrid seed from the agro-shop, everyone does that now, you can't save hybrid maize seed.

Pesticides — I spray herbicide on the wheat in spring against the broadleaf weeds, and on maize after planting. If aphids come bad on the wheat I'll spray, but usually I wait and see. Can't afford to spray for nothing.
